item.title: SciVision Vision SDK
item.description:
SciVision视觉开发包 is OPT’s industrial vision SDK for building deployable machine-vision applications around cameras, 2D/3D measurement, deep-learning inference, robot guidance, and production-line communication. It sits below visual workflow software such as Smart3 and exposes the algorithm layer directly for engineering teams that need C++/C#/Python/VB integration.

Official product feature overview: 2D, 3D, deep learning, secondary development, cross-platform deployment, controls, communications, and multi-language support.

Product role

SciVision is positioned as a full-function development kit rather than a single algorithm library. The official product page presents it as a platform for 2D vision, 3D vision, and deep learning, with GPU acceleration, multithreading, instruction-set optimization, more than 300 algorithm APIs, and cross-platform support across Windows, MacOS, Ubuntu, CentOS, and Arm.

Architecture

The SDK is organized around an application-development layer, controls and communication modules, and a broad algorithm layer. It is intended to help teams move from proof-of-concept scripts to production applications with reusable UI controls, measurement tools, communication adapters, and sample projects.

Official architecture graphic showing the SDK’s development modules and algorithm coverage.

Engineering capabilities

The product material highlights fast calls into both interface and algorithm layers, rich example projects, image controls, CPK/GRR controls, TCP/serial/PLC communication, and multi-language bindings. For production use, the practical value is that image acquisition, measurement, inspection, result visualization, and factory communication can be developed within one SDK surface.

Official heterogeneous-computing benchmark slide for SDK-side acceleration.

Companion book and examples

The companion repository at WillPanSUTD/mvbook contains Machine Vision Algorithms: Principles and Industrial Practice, a bilingual Quarto book with 42 chapters, 9 parts, dual HTML/PDF output, and runnable SciVision SDK C++ examples. The book explains the algorithms independently from the API, then connects them back to SciVision examples where code-level implementation details matter.

The mvbook repository links algorithm principles, industrial cases, and runnable SciVision SDK C++ examples.

item.title: OPT 3D Camera Product Line
item.description:
OPT’s 3D camera portfolio is organized around the major industrial sensing routes: laser profile cameras for scanning and micrometer-level measurement, projected structured-light cameras for one-shot high-precision reconstruction, speckle/RGB-D cameras for large field-of-view depth and color capture, and ToF cameras for high-frame-rate perception.

Product matrix covering laser profile, projected structured light, speckle structured light, and ToF cameras.

Product architecture

The product line is designed as a hardware and software suite rather than a set of isolated sensors. Camera families cover close-range high-precision measurement, large-format depth acquisition, 2D/3D aligned inspection, and robot guidance. The Smart3 algorithm platform connects the camera output to visual workflow design, point-cloud processing, measurement tools, and production deployment.

The portfolio compares laser triangulation, temporal coded structured light, and binocular speckle depth sensing.

Technology routes

Laser profile cameras emphasize mature motion-assisted measurement with um-level precision. Projected structured light emphasizes one-shot reconstruction and high repeatability for static or indexed parts. Speckle/RGB-D cameras emphasize wide field-of-view capture, RGB-depth alignment, and cost-effective logistics or robot-vision use cases.

Different routes are positioned by speed, precision, and application scenarios.

System deployment

The camera line is paired with the Smart3 visual algorithm platform, allowing inspection workflows to be configured with camera acquisition, preprocessing, point-cloud reconstruction, measurement, defect detection, and user-defined visualization.

Hardware: OPT 3D camera series. Software: Smart3 algorithm platform.

Industry coverage

The source deck positions the product line for lithium batteries, 3C electronics, photovoltaic, semiconductor, automotive, robotics, food, medicine, chemical, and warehouse automation scenarios, with applications including glue inspection, PCB measurement, welding inspection, dimensional checking, robot guidance, and volume measurement.

Industrial application coverage across more than 30 market segments.

item.title: OPT 3D Algorithm Platform
item.description:
The 3D algorithm platform connects OPT camera hardware to production workflows. It covers 3D imaging, point-cloud and mesh processing, defect inspection, geometric measurement, 3D matching, pose estimation, and robot guidance.

A 3D vision-guided robotic sorting workflow: image acquisition, instance segmentation, point-cloud generation, grasp-pose computation, eye-to-hand calibration, and robotic sorting.

3D imaging

The imaging layer turns raw optical observations into usable depth, height, range, and point-cloud data. It includes laser-profile extraction, structured-light reconstruction, RGB-D alignment, phase processing, depth-map generation, and point-cloud color mapping.

Structured-light reconstruction and height rendering for surface geometry and local defects.

RGB-D/3D alignment creates point-cloud data that remains registered to visual features and codes on the part.

3D processing

The processing layer prepares raw 3D data for downstream decisions. It includes point-cloud denoising, mesh segmentation, smoothing, normal estimation, region mapping, hole filling, and pose/viewpoint resampling. These tools are used when a production scene contains outliers, occlusions, vibration, or nonuniform point density.

Segmentation-driven mesh denoising preserves feature regions while suppressing noise.

Detection and inspection

Inspection algorithms use 3D geometry together with intensity or RGB cues to detect missed welds, broken welds, pinholes, blowholes, dents, scratches, bumps, glue defects, foreign objects, and surface deviations. The same stack can feed rule-based 3D thresholds or AI-assisted segmentation depending on the application.

3D defect inspection for lithium-battery welds and other reflective industrial surfaces.

Measurement

The measurement layer turns point clouds and range images into production values: gap width, step height, flatness, parallelism, volume, profile deviation, reference-plane distance, and GD&T-style evaluations. It is designed to keep geometric measurement and inspection decisions in the same coordinate frame.

Point-cloud cleaning, module segmentation, convex-hull/reference-plane construction, and side-view measurement.

Matching and pose

The matching layer supports CAD-assisted matching, point-cloud stitching, IVD/ICP matching, feature-based registration, and 6D pose estimation. In robot-facing workflows, viewpoint encoding and codebook search can turn a sparse observation into an object pose hypothesis for verification and grasp planning.

Viewpoint sampling, synthetic rendering, viewpoint encoding, and codebook lookup for 6D object pose estimation.

Robotic guidance

Robot applications combine instance segmentation, 3D point-cloud extraction, grasp-pose computation, eye-to-hand calibration, and motion execution. The same 3D algorithm stack supports unordered bin picking, logistics sorting, depalletizing, and high-throughput pick-and-place cells.

Robotic sorting cell driven by 3D perception and grasp-pose computation.

End-to-end pipeline from image acquisition to robotic arm sorting.

item.title: OPT Laser Profile 3D Cameras
item.description:
The laser profile camera family targets motion-assisted 3D measurement and inspection. The deck groups the line into LPE2, LPF2, and LPH2 series, with 21 model options, scan widths from 7 mm to 2600 mm, X-axis profile density up to 6400 points, and sampling up to 54 kHz.

LPE2, LPF2, and LPH2 line-laser camera families.

Principle

The system follows laser triangulation. A cylindrical lens spreads the laser into a line on the target surface; reflected light is imaged by CMOS; the displacement and shape of the stripe are converted into profile height. The camera then outputs depth, point cloud, and intensity data for downstream measurement.

Laser triangulation and profile extraction pipeline.

Product strengths

The series emphasizes robust profile extraction, high frame rate, dense X-axis sampling, integrated operation without an external controller, and software pairing with Smart3. The source deck highlights HDR fusion, vibration correction, stray-light suppression, peak sensitivity tuning, preprocessing, height correction, and profile post-processing.

Core capability summary for line-laser 3D cameras.

Algorithms

The line-laser workflow combines subpixel center extraction, HDR fusion, noise filtering, peak sensitivity adjustment, vibration correction, and point-cloud post-processing. These are especially important for dark plastic, reflective metal, glue surfaces, and narrow weld structures where stripe returns are unstable.

HDR fusion improves profile completeness on mixed dark and reflective materials.

Stray-light suppression and peak sensitivity tuning reduce false profile points.

Applications

Representative applications include battery weld dimension inspection, transparent glue volume calibration, dispensing path guidance, 3D defect inspection, step-height measurement, gap-width measurement, and full-coverage multi-camera inspection.

Glue-output volume calibration and transparent adhesive profile correction.

Battery weld defect inspection with aligned 2D intensity and 3D depth data.

item.title: OPT Projected Structured-Light 3D Cameras
item.description:
The projected structured-light series targets high-precision one-shot reconstruction without a motion platform. It is positioned for dimensional measurement, positioning, bin picking, semiconductor, 3C, lithium battery, and automotive component inspection.

Projected structured-light product matrix covering FPB and FPC series.

Principle

The camera projects encoded structured light onto the target, captures the deformed stripe or fringe pattern, and reconstructs 3D contour data through decoding, unwrapping, and geometric calibration. The product line is designed for rapid imaging and stable reconstruction under industrial production constraints.

Structured-light projection, encoded patterns, and 3D reconstruction.

Product strengths

The product deck highlights one-shot imaging, no motion-platform requirement, hardware-side point-cloud output, high-quality projected stripes, multi-projector fusion, multi-exposure fusion, denoising, hole filling, and Smart3 deployment.

Dual projection and telecentric imaging

The high-precision dual-projector route reduces dead zones by projecting from multiple directions. The deck reports a 95 percent reduction in imaging blind spots and uses telecentric optics to improve edge stability and Z repeatability in macro measurement tasks.

Dual-projector point-cloud fusion reduces directional blind spots.

2D and 3D alignment

The structured-light products support pixel-level 2D/3D alignment so the same acquisition can serve recognition, defect localization, and 3D measurement. This is useful when classical measurement, AI detection, and point-cloud analysis need to share the same coordinate frame.

Pixel-aligned 2D and 3D output for inspection and measurement.

Applications

Typical applications include toothbrush or workpiece bin picking, headset and sidewall dispensing guidance, semiconductor pin inspection, sealing nail weld inspection, smartphone middle-frame inspection, and high-precision surface bump or dent detection.

One-shot 3D data supports segmentation and robot picking in unordered scenes.

item.title: OPT Speckle Structured-Light RGB-D Cameras
item.description:
The speckle structured-light camera family is built around binocular depth sensing with active speckle projection. It is positioned for large field-of-view imaging, synchronized RGB-depth acquisition, and cost-sensitive industrial robot vision where millimeter-level depth is enough but speed and coverage matter.

LSA1 binocular speckle product series for large field-of-view RGB-D acquisition.

Principle

The camera projects a speckle pattern onto the scene, captures the deformed pattern from two CMOS sensors, and reconstructs depth through stereo matching and triangulation. The output can include RGB image, depth map, and colored point cloud.

Active speckle projection and binocular disparity reconstruction.

Product strengths

The source deck highlights large field-of-view coverage, low cost in wide-area scenarios, RGB image and depth map output from one acquisition, compact body design, high frame rate up to 20 FPS, and anti-ambient-light capability above 30000 lx.

Depth and RGB are aligned for colored point-cloud output and recognition-driven measurement.

Stereo algorithms

The RGB-D algorithm stack uses stereo rectification, cost computation, cost aggregation, disparity estimation, subpixel refinement, flying-point removal, consistency checks, uniqueness checks, smoothing, and 2D/3D coordinate alignment.

Stereo matching and post-processing improve edge reconstruction and flying-point removal.

Applications

Primary applications include logistics bin picking, dynamic parcel sorting, depalletizing, large-format volume measurement, PACK packaging, sheet-metal cutting localization, and robot obstacle-aware guidance. The source deck reports logistics cases with large field of view, fast point-cloud output, RGB-assisted AI recognition, and high-throughput picking.

Large field-of-view point-cloud capture for unordered logistics bin picking.

RGB-D sensing supports dynamic conveyor sorting and package classification.
